initial.name: agent_dispatch
initial.description: Dispatch a child agent for one task onto one registered git worktree: the controller dispatches a lead, and a lead dispatches workers inside its approved plugin scopes. Name the task id, the plugin scope, and the worktree id (get worktree ids from worktree_create or the host), and pass a briefing prompt for a fresh dispatch — the briefing is queued only after the child is published. Every result carries ack: what the child's own durable log proves about the task (briefed while pending, claimed while executing, terminal with the turn's recorded ending — completed means the task finished cleanly, dropped when the briefing was cancelled unrun). If this task already has a dispatched child, the tool refuses and names it: pass retry: true to reuse that child instead, which never re-delivers the briefing and reports the task's current ack, or pass followup: true with a new prompt to continue that child with explicit instructions. The engine owns the child's lifecycle and the hierarchy owns every denial; refusals name the cause and the fix.

role.description: The child's hierarchy role: 'lead' from the controller, or 'worker' from a lead.

taskId.description: The task this child owns; one task has at most one dispatched child.

pluginId.description: The plugin scope the child works under; a lead's worker scope must be in that lead's approved set.

worktreeId.description: The registered worktree id the child will own as its single writer, from worktree_create or the host.

prompt.description: The task briefing queued to a freshly dispatched child after publication. Never re-sent on a retry; with followup: true it is the continuation instructions for the existing child instead.

retry.description: Pass true to reuse the child this task already has instead of dispatching a new one; no briefing is queued on reuse.

followup.description: Pass true with a prompt to deliver explicit continuation instructions to the child this task already has: the instructions queue as the child's next ordinary turn and wake it. Requires an existing dispatched child; a fresh dispatch never queues a followup.

childId.description: The preallocated session id for the child, when the deployment configures one (the leadPluginScopes approved sets are keyed by these ids). Omitted, the engine allocates the identity.
